input.summary: Seven expert lenses map Meridian's highest-value use-case patterns; six are active, all blocked by foundational evidence gaps.
covers: Governed data foundation for AI / LLM automation pattern
Payment integrity and leakage reduction pattern

story.meaning: Six active expert lenses represent Meridian's highest-priority value patterns, but every lens is blocked by the same cluster of missing foundations: no certified medallion architecture, no identity spine, no formal governance, and no AI audit trail.
story.observed: All seven lenses are source-backed at 94% confidence. Six are active; one (end-to-end cost transparency) remains candidate. Twelve discrete foundational gaps span the top four lenses alone, with lakehouse and AI governance carrying the heaviest dependency load.
story.matters: Without closing the shared foundational gaps — medallion architecture, identity spine, semantic layer, and governance operating model — none of the six active lenses can advance from planning to decision grade, stalling CEO, CFO, and CDAO strategic priorities simultaneously.
story.supports: Prioritizing the four shared infrastructure gates (lakehouse foundation, governance model, semantic layer, identity spine) unlocks the maximum number of lenses in parallel and is the highest-leverage executive decision available.

findings: Six of seven lenses are active and source-backed, yet all share the same four foundational blockers — resolving them in sequence unlocks the entire lens portfolio rather than one use case at a time.
The unified clinical + claims lakehouse lens is the prerequisite platform for four of the remaining six lenses; its evidence closure is the single highest-leverage action on Meridian's roadmap.

Payment integrity and call center optimization are independently valuable but each carry lens-specific blockers — SAS model lineage and transcript governance respectively — that must be resolved in addition to shared infrastructure gaps.
End-to-end cost transparency is the only candidate-status lens; provider contract digitization is its sole lens-specific gate and is the largest single blocker cited by CEO, CFO, and CDAO.

breakdown.title: Expert Lens Status vs. Foundational Gate Exposure

rows.label: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
rows.note: 4 shared gates + identity spine; prerequisite for 4 other lenses

rows.label: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM
rows.note: 4 shared gates + AI audit trail + data quality rules; blocks all AI use cases

rows.label: Payment Integrity & Leakage Reduction
rows.note: SAS lineage + provider entity resolution + recovery workflow ungoverned

rows.label: Call Center Optimization
rows.note: Transcript governance + real-time CRM + intent taxonomy + member identity unproven

rows.label: End-to-End Cost Transparency

chain: Expert Lenses → Lakehouse Foundation (medallion architecture, identity spine, claims/pharmacy harmonization)
Lakehouse Foundation → AI / LLM Governance (semantic layer, audit trail, data quality rules)
AI / LLM Governance → Provider Quality & Performance + Automated Close & Reporting
Call Center Optimization → CRM real-time integration + transcript governance (parallel track)
Payment Integrity → SAS model lineage + provider entity resolution (parallel track)
relationships.note: The lakehouse and governance lenses form a sequential dependency spine that gates four downstream lenses; call center and payment integrity run as parallel tracks with their own lens-specific evidence gates that must be resolved concurrently to avoid roadmap serialization.

gaps.missing: No certified medallion architecture or AWS/Databricks foundation evidence
gaps.blocks: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse lens cannot advance; cascades to four dependent lenses
gaps.needed: Epic Clarity medallion build certification + AWS/Databricks platform readiness evidence
gaps.handoff: CDAO and CIO must co-own platform certification gate before any lens enters execution

gaps.missing: No formal data governance operating model or certified semantic layer
gaps.blocks: All seven lenses; AI/LLM automation lens specifically also lacks audit trail and data quality rule evidence
gaps.needed: Governance operating model charter + semantic layer ownership assignment + AI audit trail design
gaps.handoff: CDAO leads governance model; CFO and CMO must sign off on semantic ownership boundaries

gaps.missing: No patient/member identity spine loaded; claims and pharmacy harmonization unproven
gaps.blocks: Lakehouse lens and call center optimization lens (member identity linkage)
gaps.needed: Identity spine build and certification + claims/pharmacy harmonization evidence
gaps.handoff: Health Plan Ops and Clinical Ops must jointly certify identity resolution rules

gaps.missing: Provider contract terms not in governed digital form; attribution ownership unproven
gaps.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency lens (candidate status) and provider quality lens
gaps.needed: Contract digitization program + attribution ownership certification
gaps.handoff: Network Contracting and Finance must deliver digitized contract evidence before lens advances to active

gaps.missing: Transcript governance, intent taxonomy, and real-time CRM integration unproven
gaps.blocks: Call center optimization lens cannot advance to agent-assist or next-best-action stage
gaps.needed: Transcript governance policy + intent taxonomy certification + CRM real-time integration proof
gaps.handoff: Chief Experience Officer and CIO co-own; contact center platform team must deliver integration evidence
